newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-KHUMALO PAYS THE PRICE FOR HIS SLUMP IN FORM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KHUMALO PAYS THE PRICE FOR HIS SLUMP IN FORM.

text.p: South Africa have omitted long-standing midfielder Doctor Khumalo from their squad to play Zambia in an African zone World Cup qualifier in Lusaka on January 11.

He has been a member of the South African team since the country's return from apartheid-enforced isolation in 1992, scoring South Africa's first international goal after 30 years and playing a prominent role in the African Nations' Cup victory in February.
But a recent slump in form for Khumalo, who enjoys pop star status in the country, has seen coach Clive Barker leave him out of the 19-man squad for the vital match in Lusaka.
Barker also left out striker Mark Williams, scorer of both goals in South Africa's 2-0 win in the Nations' Cup final against Tunisia. Williams recently signed for Brazilian club Corinthians.
Only one uncapped player -- striker Pollen Ndlanya -- was named in the squad, which includes eight European-based professionals.
South Africa share the lead in group three, after beating Zaire 1-0 in November, with Congo, surprise 1-0 winners over the Zambians in their opening match.
Goalkeepers - Mark Anderson (Umtata Bucks), Andre Arendse (Cape Town Spurs)
Defenders - Mark Fish (Lazio, Italy), Sizwe Motaung, David Nyathi (St Gallen, Switzerland), Lucas Radebe (Leeds, England), Neil Tovey, Jacob Tshisevhe (Kaizer Chiefs)

Midfielders - Linda Buthelezi (Mamelodi Sundowns), John Moshoeu (Kocaelispor, Turkey), Thomas Madigage (Supersport United), Helman Mkhalele, Dumisa Ngobe (Orlando Pirates), Eric Tinkler (Cagliari, Italy)
Strikers - Brendan Augustine (Linzer ASK, Austria), Shaun Bartlett (AmaZulu), Phil Masinga (Salernitana, Italy), Pollen Ndlanya (Kaizer Chiefs), Jerry Sikhosana (Orlando Pirates)
